rationale: All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported all align to abdominal aortic aneurysm). PGS000753 is best supported because it provides the clearest PRS-comparable discriminative evidence via an effect size (OR per SD 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) alongside basic covariates (age, sex, PCs) and a disease-focused publication context (MVP AAA genetics), whereas most others primarily report full-model AUROC/C-index without PRS-only isolation. Runners-up are the two disease-focused Nat Genet PRS-CS scores (PGS003972/PGS003973) from a large AAA GWAS meta-analysis with genome-wide shrinkage and consistent endpoint alignment; however, their reported metrics are full-model (AUROC 0.69; C-index 0.882) with limited PRS-only comparability and unknown/variable covariate reporting, so they remain less directly interpretable than the OR-based evidence in PGS000753. Overall confidence is moderated because across the pool PRS-only AUC is absent and several reported high full-model discrimination values are likely covariate-driven per the provided domain guidance, limiting clean cross-model performance comparison. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 4 candidates are direct matches to the target concept (alcohol dependence / alcohol use disorder), with endpoint fidelity supported by phenotyping_reported being AUD/AUD criteria count and trait_efo mapping to alcohol dependence/alcohol dependence measurement. PGS002738 is best supported because it is explicitly labeled Alcohol use disorder with trait_efo=alcohol dependence, uses a modern genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS), has a reasonably large validation sample (n=7,900), and reports a relatively strong discriminative effect size (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96, 95% CI 1.54–2.51). Main limitation: covariates are unknown and there are no PRS-comparable AUC/R2 metrics reported, so cross-model comparability is limited.

Runners-up: (1) PGS002739 is also an explicit AUD/alcohol dependence model and reports a supportive effect size (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.76, 95% CI 1.32–2.34) with a sizable validation (n=6,315), but it is evaluated only in African American/Afro-Caribbean ancestry and uses a gene-based PRS-CSx variant with far fewer variants (858), making it less broadly supported without a specified deployment ancestry. (2) PGS000201 is a direct AUD-criteria-count phenotype (DSM-5 criteria count, log-transformed) and uses PRS-CS with very large variant count (~1.09M) and basic covariates; it reports ΔR2 vs covariates (0.01192) and beta, but the effect-size evidence is weaker than PGS002738’s OR-based stratification and it is framed as “Problematic alcohol use” rather than explicit AUD, lowering endpoint specificity slightly. PGS000202 is the weakest of the set due to smaller validation (n=1,251) and smaller ΔR2 (0.00456) with otherwise similar phenotype framing.

All three candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo = alcoholic liver cirrhosis / near-synonymous labels). PGS004913 is best supported because its phenotyping_reported is explicitly alcohol-associated liver cirrhosis (highest endpoint fidelity), it is disease-focused (heavy drinkers) with standard covariates (age/sex/PCs), and it reports PRS-comparable signal via an R²=0.029 plus an OR (top vs bottom PRS deciles)=4.4. Remaining limitation: the reported R² appears to be a full-model/unspecified R² (not explicitly PGS-only), and no AUROC/C-index is provided, so cross-model comparability is limited.

Runner-up PGS001777 remains strongly endpoint-aligned (cirrhosis alcohol related) and reports an AUROC=0.671 plus a large stratification OR (top 20% vs bottom 20%)=6.18, but it is a very sparse 3-variant score, has unknown covariates, and has a small validation sample (n=1,390), lowering robustness.

Second runner-up PGS000704 is endpoint-aligned (Alcoholic cirrhosis) and has large validation (n=135,300) with basic covariates, but its only visible discrimination metric is a full-model C-index=0.711 (not PGS-only) and the per-SD HR=1.18 suggests relatively weak PRS-only signal; it also comes from a broad biomarker genetics paper rather than a cirrhosis-focused PRS study, reducing confidence in disease-optimized performance.

All 19 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (angina pectoris) via trait_efo and phenotype labels (Angina / I20 / PheCode 411.3), so a direct-match exists. Among the UKB snpnet models from the same publication family (PGS001260/PGS001261/PGS001262), PGS001262 has the strongest reported full-model discrimination (AUROC 0.80729 with age/sex/array/PC covariates) and the highest incremental AUROC (0.0098) plus the highest PGS-only metrics in that sibling set (PGS-only AUROC 0.58683; PGS-only R2 0.01304), making it the best-supported choice on comparable PRS-relevant evidence. Runners-up are PGS001261 (time-to-event angina pectoris; slightly lower PGS-only AUROC/R2 and incremental AUROC than PGS001262) and PGS001260 (similar endpoint but weaker metrics than the other two). Confidence is not High because the strongest full-model AUROC is partly covariate-driven by design, and several newer non-framework candidates (e.g., PGS004457/PGS004527, PGS005048/PGS005052/PGS005057/PGS005058) report only full-model C-index or OR without clear PRS-only metrics, limiting cross-family comparability from the visible metadata.

All 9 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo=ankylosing spondylitis; phenotyping_reported is ankylosing spondylitis or a closely related TTE definition). Among them, PGS002089 is best supported on PRS-comparable performance evidence: it reports the strongest available PRS-only-like metric in this pool (partial correlation partial-r=0.0919, CI 0.0775–0.1063) from the UKB portability study, and it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with a large variant set (22,026), which is structurally favorable versus very sparse models. Runners-up: PGS001267 and PGS001268 provide explicit PRS-only AUROC and PRS-only R² (and incremental AUROC) with basic covariates, but they come from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework ("across 813 traits") and are extremely sparse (10 variants), which domain guidance flags as a generalization risk; between the two, both are similarly supported, with PGS001268 slightly higher full-model AUROC/R² but a time-to-event phenotype. Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL because the top candidate’s performance reporting is limited to partial-r (no AUROC/R²), while the candidates with explicit PRS-only AUROC/R² are from a pan-trait sparse framework with very low variant counts, leaving meaningful uncertainty in selecting a clearly strongest direct-match model.

Direct-match candidates for aortic stenosis are present (PGS005252, PGS005254) and closely related aortic valve function proxies with the same stated phenotyping of incident aortic stenosis are also present (PGS005255, PGS005256). PGS005252 is best supported because it is an exact trait match (trait_reported/trait_efo = aortic stenosis) with endpoint-faithful phenotyping (incident aortic stenosis cases) and it provides the richest comparable performance evidence in the visible set (reported C-index 0.87 plus HR 1.92) alongside a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDPred2) and large validation (n=446,895), albeit with a relatively heavy clinical covariate bundle that makes the reported C-index potentially covariate-influenced. Runner-up PGS005254 is also an exact aortic stenosis model with incident endpoint and a strong HR (1.64, CI provided) and a large training sample (n=205,483), but it lacks reported discrimination metrics (no AUC/C-index/R2 shown) and has less extensive covariate adjustment detail. For the second runner-up, PGS005255 is selected over PGS005256 because both are proxy trait_reported models (mean pressure gradient vs peak aortic velocity) but share the same stated phenotyping (incident aortic stenosis) and covariates; PGS005255 has slightly stronger visible effect-size evidence (HR 1.53 with CI 1.40–1.66 vs HR 1.53 with CI 1.41–1.67). Confidence is Moderate because none of the aortic stenosis candidates report clearly PRS-only (covariate-free) discrimination metrics, and the strongest discrimination metric available (PGS005252 C-index) is reported in a full model with multiple clinical covariates, limiting cross-model comparability. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

Direct-match candidates for the target trait (arthritis) are present, including PGS001135 ("Arthritis (nos)", trait_efo=arthritis) and two "Other arthritis" models (PGS004477, PGS004547; trait_efo=arthritis). PGS001135 is the most endpoint-faithful to generic arthritis risk (phenotyping_reported="Arthritis (nos)") and provides PRS-comparable metrics (PGS AUROC (no covariates)=0.53928; PGS R2 (no covariates)=0.00291) plus incremental AUROC, enabling interpretation beyond a covariate-driven full-model AUROC. However, it comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework ("Significant sparse polygenic risk scores across 813 traits"), which domain guidance flags as tending to underperform disease-focused scores in external validation, and its PRS-only metrics are modest—so overall support is not strong enough for a high-quality designation. The runners-up (PGS004547, then PGS004477) are also direct matches (trait_efo=arthritis; phenotyping_reported="M13 (Other arthritis)") but have limited comparable performance evidence (only an OR reported, no PRS-only AUROC/R2 shown) and unknown covariates, making them harder to justify over PGS001135 despite being non-813-traits framework models.

Direct-match candidates for asthma are abundant. PGS002727 is best supported overall because it is explicitly phenotype-aligned to asthma in a disease-focused context ("Multiancestral polygenic risk score for pediatric asthma"; phenotyping_reported="Pediatric asthma"), reports a strong PRS effect size (OR=1.57 per SD, 95% CI 1.55–1.60) and a reasonable full-model AUROC (0.66 with R²=0.04), and is evaluated at very large scale (validation n=391,820) across multiple ancestries (EVAL includes AFR/AMR/EAS/EUR/SAS). Main limitation: endpoint is pediatric-specific rather than generic asthma, and covariates are listed as Unknown, which lowers comparability confidence.

Runners-up: (1) PGS001782 (Cell Genom global biobank PRS-CS-auto) is a direct asthma endpoint with genome-wide shrinkage and multi-biobank training; it reports PRS-comparable R² (Nagelkerke’s R² covariates-regressed-out=0.048844) and AUROC=0.659 in EUR evaluation, providing relatively clean PRS signal evidence, but it comes from a broad framework-style paper and has smaller validation (n=7,128) than PGS002727. (2) PGS001344 (snpnet; asthma diagnosed by doctor) has strong endpoint fidelity (doctor-diagnosed asthma) and the best full-model AUROC among the snpnet siblings shown (full_model_auc=0.66621; incremental AUROC reported 0.07977; PGS-only AUROC 0.64568), but it is from the pan-trait UKB "813 traits" framework family, which domain guidance penalizes versus disease-focused models when available.

All 6 candidates are direct EFO matches to atopic eczema, but several have endpoint mismatches: PGS003459/PGS003486/PGS004903 are evaluated on paradoxical eczema in biologic-treated psoriasis (therapy-/context-specific rather than generic atopic eczema), lowering endpoint fidelity for the target trait. Among the remaining endpoint-faithful models, PGS002755 and PGS004587 both use an incident atopic dermatitis endpoint with very large European evaluation (n=337,910) and report HR (high vs low PRS) estimates (1.249 for PGS002755; 1.153 for PGS004587), providing directly comparable PRS effect evidence; PGS002755 is preferred due to the stronger reported HR and a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with ~1.09M variants (structurally favorable for polygenic traits). PGS001773 targets moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis (subtype/severity restriction) and reports a very high full-model AUROC (0.93) and R² (0.49), but these are full-model metrics (not PRS-only) and appear implausibly high relative to the provided heritability ceiling guidance, so they are discounted; additionally it is a 25-variant score, which is structurally sparse for a polygenic trait. Overall confidence is moderate (not high) because none of the candidates report PRS-only AUROC/R², and key comparisons rely on effect sizes and endpoint alignment rather than clean PRS-comparable discrimination metrics.

All listed candidates are direct matches to atrial fibrillation (or AF/flutter), so ranking hinges on endpoint fidelity plus PRS-comparable evidence and study archetype. PGS005168 is best supported because it is a disease-focused AF meta-analysis score (Nat Genet 2025) with direct AF phenotyping, basic covariates (age/sex/array plus CHARGE-AF adjustment), and strong reported discrimination (C-index 0.8718 with CI) alongside a strong per-SD HR (~1.67), with extensive performance record support (record_count 45) and large validation (n=52,757). The main limitation is that the reported C-index appears to be a full-model metric (not explicitly PRS-only), and inclusion of CHARGE-AF suggests some risk-wrapper covariate packaging that can inflate full-model discrimination, so confidence is not High.

Runner-up PGS005313 is also disease-focused (Nat Commun 2025), uses a strong modern cross-ancestry method (PRS-CSx), reports strong effect size (OR 1.82 with tight CI) and AUROC 0.78 with CI, and has broad multi-cohort development; however, its evaluation is MAE-only (100%) and the selected validation ancestry string is mixed/unspecific, making direct comparability and portability less clear from the visible metadata.

Second runner-up PGS002814 (Nat Genet 2023) is a very large cross-ancestry AF GWAS-derived score with strong reported OR (~1.94) and AUROC 0.74, but its development/validation context is East-Asian-focused (DEV MAE; EVAL EAS 100%), which is a limitation for generic AF deployment when no target ancestry is specified in the context. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 4 visible candidates are direct matches to the target trait (atrial flutter) via trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported, but overall evidence quality is limited by study archetype and metric comparability. PGS001263 is the only exact-label atrial flutter model and reports explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC (no covariates)=0.61716; PGS R2 (no covariates)=0.02517), enabling a heritability sanity check (PGS-only R2 remains below the provided h2_obs=0.0157 / h2_liability=0.1443 ceiling guidance, though scale differences mean this is only a coarse check). However, it comes from a pan-trait UKB framework paper (“Significant sparse polygenic risk scores across 813 traits…”) using a sparse snpnet model, which domain guidance flags as tending to generalize poorly; its high full-model AUROC (0.78179) is also not treated as PRS-comparable. Runner-up PGS001339 is very similar (same framework paper/method/covariates) but is a combined AF+flutter time-to-event endpoint rather than flutter-only, with slightly lower PRS-only AUROC/R2, so it ranks behind PGS001263. For the second runner-up, PGS002050 (LDpred2, genome-wide, 554,908 variants) is structurally stronger than PGS001841 (penalized regression, 3,980 variants) within the same “Portability of 245 polygenic scores…” family, and has slightly higher partial-r (0.1034 vs 0.1026), but both lack PRS-only AUROC/R2, limiting confidence and preventing a clear high-quality designation.

Two direct-match candidates are present (both map to autism spectrum disorder). PGS000327 is best supported because its phenotyping_reported is explicitly "Autism spectrum disorder" (highest endpoint fidelity), it comes from an ASD-focused Nat Genet study, and it reports supportive PRS signal (OR per SD 1.33 with R²=0.0245 in European validation), with only basic covariates (genetic PCs, genotyping wave). PGS002790 has weaker endpoint fidelity because phenotyping_reported is "Psychiatric behavior (withdrawn)" despite trait_reported/efo being ASD, and its reported partial R² is lower (0.00546) with no effect sizes shown; it also lacks clear training sample information (N/A) and appears embedded in a broader cross-disorder/sex-specific context. Overall confidence is limited to Moderate because neither model reports clearly PRS-only metrics (the R² fields appear as full_model/partial R²), and both are EUR-only evaluation, constraining generalizability evidence.

All 20 visible candidates are direct matches to basal cell carcinoma by trait_efo/trait_reported, but they vary in endpoint fidelity and strength of reported PRS signal. PGS000452 is best supported because it has a clean, direct BCC endpoint (phenotyping_reported: Basal cell carcinoma), basic covariates (age/sex/batch/PCs), and the strongest visible PRS-discrimination evidence among the comparable endpoint-faithful models (per-SD OR=1.663 [1.57–1.761], full-model AUROC=0.632, and the largest reported Nagelkerke R² in this set at 0.0487). The two closest runners-up are PGS000454 and PGS000456, which share the same direct BCC endpoint and similarly basic covariates, with essentially tied full-model AUROC (0.632 and 0.63) and nearly identical per-SD ORs (~1.66 and ~1.63) and R² (~0.0489 and ~0.0456). Confidence is Moderate because (i) the AUROC values shown are full-model (not explicitly PGS-only), limiting cross-model comparability, and (ii) several near-clone PRSweb/Cancer PRSweb models have very similar endpoint/covariate context and performance, making the top choice only marginally separated by the available metrics. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All three candidates are direct matches to the target trait via trait_efo/trait_reported. PGS001824 is preferred because it has the most endpoint-faithful labeling and phenotyping for the target ("Disorders of bilirubin excretion"; trait_efo exactly "bilirubin metabolism disease"), and it avoids the time-to-event framing seen in PGS000924. Between the two same-endpoint siblings (PGS001824 vs PGS002032), the visible performance evidence (partial-r 0.0716 with similar CI) and study context are essentially identical, so selection is limited by lack of differentiating PRS-comparable metrics (no PGS-only AUROC/R²) and no external (non-UKB) development/validation evidence in the metadata; this keeps confidence below High. PGS002032 is the closest runner-up as the same endpoint from the same publication family, with a more genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) and far higher variant count, but without stronger reported performance it cannot clearly outrank PGS001824. PGS000924 ranks third despite reporting strong-looking AUC/R², because it comes from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework ("across 813 traits"; snpnet with only 5 variants) and uses a broader combined endpoint (porphyrin + bilirubin metabolism) with time-to-event phenotyping, which domain guidance flags as less reliable for external performance and endpoint fidelity. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All three candidates are direct matches to the target trait family (bipolar disorder) via trait_reported/trait_efo (bipolar disorder; bipolar I; bipolar II) and share the same publication, method (SDPR), EUR-only GWAS/EVAL ancestry, similar variant counts (~935k–949k), and similar basic covariates (age, PCs1-3). However, endpoint fidelity is unclear/possibly misaligned for all three because phenotyping_reported fields are non-diagnostic behavioral/cognitive measures rather than bipolar disorder case/control status, and the only reported metric is a small full_model_r2/partial R² (no PRS-only AUC/R²), limiting comparability and strength of evidence. Given near-indistinguishable metadata and uncertain phenotype alignment, PGS002786 is selected narrowly because it is the only model labeled as the broad target ('Bipolar disorder' rather than subtype), while runners-up are the subtype-specific scores (PGS002787, PGS002788) with similarly weak/uncertain endpoint evidence.

All three candidates are direct matches at the EFO level for the target concept (blood coagulation disease), but endpoint fidelity differs: PGS001033 targets “Other coagulation defects” with a time-to-event phenotype, while PGS001826/PGS002034 target a specific congenital clotting-factor deficiency subtype (congenital vitamin K-dependent coagulation factors deficiency). Between the two congenital-deficiency siblings from the same publication with essentially identical phenotype/covariates and very similar partial-r performance (0.0563 vs 0.0562), PGS002034 is modestly preferred on structural grounds (LDpred2 genome-wide shrinkage with 32,552 variants vs penalized regression with 45 variants), which domain guidance treats as a positive signal when endpoints/metrics are otherwise near-identical. PGS001033 is ranked behind despite having explicit AUROC fields because it comes from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework paper (a known negative context signal in the provided domain knowledge) and is extremely sparse (1 variant), even though it reports PRS-only AUROC and uses only basic covariates. Overall outcome is sub-optimal because the best-supported option is still a subtype-specific congenital endpoint rather than a clearly comprehensive ‘blood coagulation disease’ diagnosis endpoint, and key comparable PRS-only discrimination metrics are missing for the congenital-deficiency models (only partial-r is provided). | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All three selected models are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo = breast carcinoma; phenotyping_reported = Breast cancer) and come from the same disease-focused benchmarking study family (“Evaluation of polygenic scoring methods in five biobanks…”), with empty covariates (covariates = 0), which avoids covariate-inflated full-model metrics. Among the visible candidates, PGS004153 (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV) has the strongest reported discrimination and variance explained in its selected European validation record (full_model_auc ≈ 0.6625; full_model_r2 ≈ 0.0764) and strong per-SD effect size (OR ≈ 1.83), consistent with the domain guidance that multi-score aggregation is a positive structural signal when endpoint fidelity is comparable. The runners-up PGS004040 (LDpred2.CV) and PGS004025 (LDpred2-auto) are very close on the same endpoint/covariate setting, with nearly identical AUROC/R2 and OR evidence (both ~0.6598 AUROC; ~0.0736–0.0739 R2; OR ~1.81), making them the best-supported alternatives. Confidence is Moderate because several near-tied, endpoint-identical candidates exist in this same family and the differences in AUROC/R2 between the top three are modest.

All listed candidates are direct matches to the target trait (celiac disease) via trait_efo and largely consistent phenotyping_reported. PGS000316 is best supported overall because it has an endpoint-faithful phenotype ("Coeliac disease"), reports strong discrimination (full-model AUROC=0.879 with tight CI), and is from a disease-focused clinical-care context rather than a pan-trait or portability framework; its training uses multiple cohorts (B58C, UKBS), which is mildly supportive for external orientation. Key limitation: the reported AUROC is a full-model metric with covariates listed as "Unknown", so PRS-only performance cannot be directly compared across models, lowering certainty.

Runner-up PGS000040 is also disease-focused with phenotype "Coeliac disease" and reports a very high AUROC=0.9, but this is explicitly a full-model AUROC (no PRS-only metrics) and uses a smaller training/validation context than PGS000316 in the visible metadata, making it slightly less supported.

Second runner-up PGS001301 provides explicit PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.82867; PGS-only R2=0.14224) with stated covariates and a large UKB training set, but it comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper ("across 813 traits"), which domain guidance flags as systematically less reliable than disease-focused models when such alternatives exist; additionally its phenotype label is broader ("Malabsorption/coeliac disease"). | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_efo=cervical carcinoma; phenotyping_reported is cervical cancer/incident cervical cancer). PGS003428 is best supported overall because it comes from a cervical-phenotype GWAS meta-analysis context (publication explicitly about cervical phenotypes and risk stratification), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred; 2,894,555 variants) consistent with stronger structural properties for polygenic traits, and reports a moderate per-SD effect size (HR=1.33) with basic covariates (age, smoking). Main limitation: it lacks PRS-only (no-covariate) discrimination metrics, and its reported C-index (0.613) is a full-model metric, so standalone PRS performance is uncertain.

Runner-up PGS000073: strong endpoint fidelity (incident cervical cancer) with large European evaluation (n=211,795) and reported HR=1.22 plus C-index/AUROC ~0.75, but these are full-model metrics with multiple epidemiologic covariates (parity, oral contraceptive use, pack-years), and it is a cross-cancer evaluation paper (less disease-focused than the cervical GWAS meta-analysis). Runner-up PGS005165: direct endpoint in an East Asian cohort (EAS GWAS/EVAL) with HR=1.20, offering ancestry-specific evidence not present in the EUR-only disease-focused scores, but it is a small GWAS-hits model (15 variants) with only full-model C-index (0.566), limiting inference about PRS strength.

Other candidates were deprioritized: PGS000784 is essentially a reweighting of PGS000073 (inverse weights) with near-identical metrics; PGS001299 is a pan-trait UKB framework sparse model (snpnet, 24 variants) with weak PRS-only AUROC (~0.55) and very small incremental AUROC; PGS003389 shows weak discrimination (AUROC 0.563; R² 0.00158) despite more variants than sparse models.

All 6 candidates are direct matches to cholelithiasis (either exact cholelithiasis/K80 or a closely related composite including cholecystitis). The strongest endpoint-fidelity cluster is the Commun Biol 2024 pair explicitly targeting ICD10 K80 cholelithiasis (PGS004546, PGS004476) with EUR development and EUR evaluation; within this same-endpoint/same-study family, PGS004546 is preferred because it reports a higher per-SD effect size (OR 1.2986 vs 1.2194), which is the main available discriminative signal given both lack PRS-comparable AUC/R2 and have unknown covariates. Runner-up PGS004476 is the closest sibling with identical endpoint and study context but weaker OR. For the second runner-up, PGS001174 is selected because it provides the richest PRS-comparable performance evidence (PGS-only AUROC 0.623 and PGS-only R2 0.028; incremental AUROC 0.043) and coherent covariates, but it is penalized as a pan-trait UKB framework sparse score and uses a time-to-event phenotype, which lowers confidence versus the K80 disease-coded models. Overall confidence is moderate because key comparable metrics are missing for the top-ranked Commun Biol models, and the remaining candidates (PGS001861/PGS002072 portability-framework composites; PGS005150 EAS-only evaluation) are direct but not clearly superior on the visible evidence.

All listed candidates are direct EFO matches to chronic kidney disease, so ranking hinges on endpoint fidelity plus PRS-relevant performance evidence and study archetype. PGS002237 is best supported because it is explicitly CKD stage 3+ with a clear clinical threshold phenotype (eGFR <45), comes from a CKD-focused paper (“Genome-wide polygenic score to predict chronic kidney disease across ancestries.”, Nat Med), includes multi-ancestry evaluation, and reports a strong full-model AUROC (0.78) alongside a moderate per-SD effect size (OR 1.47). Remaining limitation: the reported AUROC is full-model with many clinical covariates (e.g., hypertension, diabetes, BMI, medication use), and no PGS-only AUROC/R² is provided, so the standalone PRS contribution cannot be cleanly compared across models.

Runner-up PGS005090 is also stage 3+ CKD with strong reported discrimination (AUROC 0.9; R² 0.1) and a moderate OR (1.41), but it is evaluated only in African American/Afro-Caribbean populations (GWAS/EVAL AFR), making it less universally supported as a general best pick from the mixed-ancestry candidate set based on the visible evidence alone.

Runner-up PGS004158 (MultiPRS.CV) has the strongest full-model AUROC/R² among the large coherent “five biobanks” CKD-or-dialysis sibling cluster (AUROC ~0.592; R² ~0.020) with covariates listed as 0 (clean comparability), but that cluster’s endpoint is broader (“CKD or dialysis”) and the absolute discrimination is much lower than the disease-focused Nat Med CKD stage 3+ model; additionally, these are benchmarking-style models with relatively small development sample size (n=13,496), so they are supportive but not clearly superior.

All 10 candidates are direct matches via trait_efo=chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, with varying endpoint labels (COPD, chronic airway obstruction, ICD J44, and one emphysema subtype). PGS001783 is best supported because it is an exact COPD endpoint (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported both COPD) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS-auto) with very large variant count, plus it reports a PRS-comparable metric (Nagelkerke R2 with covariates regressed out = 0.038092) that is consistent with the provided COPD heritability ceiling (h2_liability≈0.0388), supporting that the metric is plausible and PRS-driven. Main limitation: it comes from a global biobank framework-style paper and has relatively small listed validation sample size (n=7,128) with limited per-model performance detail (single record; AUROC shown but not explicitly PRS-only).

Runners-up: PGS001788 is the closest sibling (same paper, same endpoint, same method family and genome-wide scale) but has materially lower reported covariates-regressed-out R2 (0.0163), so it ranks second. For third, PGS001332 is an exact COPD label with explicit PGS-only AUROC/R2 reported (PGS-only AUROC≈0.54; PGS-only R2≈0.00235) and basic covariates, but it is from the sparse pan-trait UKB framework (snpnet, 482 variants) which domain guidance flags as typically less externally robust than genome-wide shrinkage disease models; its PRS-only metrics are also notably weaker than the PRS-CS-auto R2 evidence. Other direct-match options (PGS001333/PGS001334) are similar sparse-framework variants with small metric differences; PGS002062/PGS001850 are portability-framework ‘chronic airway obstruction’ with partial-r only; PGS004466/PGS004536 are ICD J44 but provide only ORs with unknown covariates, limiting comparability.

All 6 candidates are direct matches to the target concept (cirrhosis of liver) via either exact cirrhosis EFO (PGS000726, PGS000776, PGS004621) or the clinically overlapping alcoholic cirrhosis subtype (PGS000704, PGS001777, PGS004913). PGS004621 is best supported because it has the cleanest phenotype alignment for the generic target (trait_efo and phenotyping_reported both ‘Cirrhosis’), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with very large variant coverage (1,089,806), and comes from a disease-focused cirrhosis genetics paper with a very large evaluation sample size (n=1,153,995) and basic covariates (age, sex, PCs). However, the evidence remains limited for a clearly high-quality pick because no PRS-only (covariate-free) AUROC/R² is reported for any candidate, and the available AUROC values are full-model metrics that are not directly comparable as standalone PRS performance.

Direct-match candidates for lung cancer are present (multiple models with trait_reported/phenotyping_reported as lung cancer or closely synonymous endpoints). All listed candidates are direct matches to lupus erythematosus via either systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) or lupus erythematosus (localized and systemic). Direct-match candidates for the target EFO term (lymphoid leukemia) are present (e.g., PGS000788, PGS000077, PGS000645, PGS002305). Runners-up: PGS000077 is a near-identical endpoint-aligned predecessor (incident lymphocytic leukemia; same evaluation n=391,338; basic covariates) but shows weaker effect size (HR=1.45) and slightly lower full-model AUROC (0.719 vs 0.738), so it ranks second. All 7 candidates are direct lexical/concept matches to macular degeneration/age-related macular degeneration, but they vary in endpoint fidelity and PRS-comparable performance evidence. PGS004606 is best supported because it is disease-endpoint aligned (phenotyping_reported: "Age-related macular degeneration"), comes from a disease-focused AMD GWAS study (Nat Genet 2024), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; ~1.0M variants), and reports supportive effect size evidence (OR 1.76 per SD) plus a full-model AUROC (0.71) with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs). Runner-up PGS004607 is from the same disease-focused study family with the same endpoint and method, but has weaker reported discrimination/effect size (full-model AUROC 0.65; OR 1.48) and a GWAS ancestry listed as AFR with EUR evaluation, making it less clearly optimal than PGS004606 given the visible evidence.

Second runner-up PGS001013 has an exact trait label match ("Macular degeneration") and uniquely reports PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.55283; PGS-only R² 0.00599) enabling PRS-comparable interpretation; however it is from a pan-trait UK Biobank sparse framework ("across 813 traits"), with a non-specific UKB phenotype string ("Eye problems/disorders Macular degeneration") and modest PRS-only performance, which domain guidance flags as typically weaker than disease-focused multi-cohort scores when available.

Direct-match candidates for melanoma are present (multiple models with trait_efo=melanoma / phenotyping_reported melanoma endpoints). PGS002247 is best supported within the visible list because it has strong endpoint fidelity (incident invasive melanoma), European evaluation ancestry, and comparatively strong reported discrimination among the incident-invasive melanoma models (full_model AUROC 0.691 with reported R² 0.072). All 6 candidates are direct lexical/EFO matches to multiple myeloma except PGS003450, which has an explicit endpoint mismatch (phenotyping_reported = Chronic lymphocytic leukemia) despite trait_reported saying Multiple myeloma, so it is deprioritized as endpoint-incoherent. Among the remaining coherent multiple-myeloma endpoints (PGS000652/653/654/002281/002306), none reports PRS-only AUROC/R2; available AUROCs are full-model and thus only weakly comparable. PGS002281 is preferred because it is disease-focused (title explicitly about multiple myeloma risk prediction), has clean phenotype alignment (phenotyping_reported = Multiple myeloma), and shows the strongest and most precisely estimated full-model AUROC in a reasonably sized European validation (AUROC 0.644, CI 0.622–0.666; n=2,395) plus a supportive risk gradient (OR highest vs lowest quintiles 3.18). Third, PGS000653 is a coherent multiple-myeloma model with basic covariates and larger validation (n=2,738) and moderate per-SD effect size (OR 1.327), but its full-model AUROC (0.577) is lower than the 2022 disease-focused scores. Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL because the key PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R2 or incremental AUROC) are missing across candidates, and several reported AUROCs are full-model values with differing/unknown covariate sets.

All 7 visible candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo=multiple sclerosis; phenotyping_reported is MS for all except PGS001271 which is explicitly time-to-event). PGS002726 is preferred because it is disease-focused (Brain paper on MS susceptibility/phenotype in Europeans, training cohort IMSGC) and reports the strongest visible discrimination signal among the disease-focused candidates (full-model AUROC=0.80 with an additional strong stratification metric OR=15.0 for top 10% vs median), whereas several other strong-method candidates lack comparable AUROC/PRS-only metrics. Runners-up: PGS000809 is also disease-focused multi-cohort (many MS cohorts listed) with basic covariates and reports full-model AUROC=0.765 plus an effect size (β=0.63) and R²=0.069; PGS002038 (LDpred2, genome-wide shrinkage with 129,077 variants) has strong structural properties and a portability-style multi-ancestry evaluation context, but only reports partial-r (0.0396) rather than AUROC/R², limiting comparability. Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL (not high-quality) because key PRS-comparable metrics are inconsistent/missing across top candidates (several report only full-model AUROC or partial-r; PGS-only metrics are not available for the disease-focused models), covariates are unknown for PGS002726, and two candidates (PGS001270/PGS001271) come from a pan-trait UKB framework paper which domain guidance flags as less reliable for external generalization despite having explicit PGS-only metrics. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

Direct-match candidates for myocardial infarction are present (multiple models with trait_efo/phenotyping_reported explicitly myocardial infarction or acute myocardial infarction). Both visible candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo = "Nasal Cavity Polyp"; phenotyping_reported = ICD10 J33 nasal polyp) and come from the same publication, cohort context (UKB), ancestry (DEV/EVAL EUR 100%), variant count (1,059,939), and validation sample size (n=56,192), so endpoint fidelity and transportability are essentially tied. Two direct-match candidates are present (both map to nicotine dependence via trait_efo and use the same endpoint wording in phenotyping_reported: Tobacco use disorder) from the same UKB portability publication, so endpoint fidelity is comparable and neither has an obvious phenotype mismatch. With no PRS-only AUC/R2 reported for either model, the main differentiators available are the PRS-comparable metric provided (partial correlation) and structural properties. PGS002037 shows higher partial-r (0.0741 vs 0.0557, both in European validation) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage-style method (LDpred2) with far more variants (847,691 vs 13,838), which is supportive for a polygenic trait when other evidence is similar. Limitation: both models come from a portability/framework-style UKB-derived study and lack standard PRS-only discrimination metrics (AUC/R2), so the evidence is not strong enough for a high-confidence pick despite the consistent advantage for PGS002037.

All 7 candidates are direct matches to the target concept (nodular goiter) via either benign nodular goiter or nontoxic multinodular goiter; however, two candidates (PGS005273, PGS005274) are case-control contrasts of thyroid carcinoma vs benign nodular goiter and are less endpoint-faithful for generic nodular goiter risk than the pure benign-goiter endpoints.

It also uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRSCS) with very large variant count (~1.09M), a positive structural signal relative to the P+T model.

Runners-up: PGS005263 is the closest sibling (same endpoint, same method family, similar variant count) with slightly weaker AUROC; PGS005261 remains endpoint-aligned but is structurally weaker (P+T, 110 variants) and has the lowest AUROC among the benign-goiter set.

Main limitation lowering this from DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY: for the 2026 benign-goiter models, only full-model AUROC is shown and covariates are “Unknown,” so the AUROC is not clearly PRS-only/comparable; meanwhile the 2022 UKB portability models (PGS001814/PGS002022) report only small partial correlations and come from a portability framework, creating uncertainty about cross-study comparability and leaving no clearly clean PRS-only metric to decisively separate candidates.

All 10 listed candidates are direct matches to the target trait (obesity) via trait_efo and/or phenotyping_reported. However, the choice remains sub-optimal because most candidates have incomplete or non-comparable performance reporting (many have null AUC/R²; some have unknown covariates; some are framework/portability-derived), making it hard to confirm superiority on directly comparable PRS-only metrics. As runners-up, PGS001298 is supported by having explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.57573; PGS R²=0.01146) and basic covariates, but is penalized by being a pan-trait UKB framework score and by a time-to-event phenotype ("TTE obesity"). PGS002033 is a direct-match portability-framework score with a stronger reported partial correlation (partial-r=0.0789) than its sibling PGS001825, and uses a genome-wide method (LDpred2) with very large variant count, but still suffers from framework-study penalties and lacks PRS-only AUROC/R².

All 13 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (osteoporosis) by trait_reported/trait_efo, with phenotype alignment generally acceptable. The main limitation is that many other candidates lack comparable PRS-only metrics (AUC/R2) and several come from framework/portability-style publications, making cross-candidate ranking uncertain.

Both visible candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo=otosclerosis). All 11 listed candidates are direct matches to the target trait (pancreatic carcinoma) via pancreatic cancer / exocrine pancreatic carcinoma endpoints, with one clinically dominant subtype (pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma; PGS002264) also plausibly aligned. However, the reported AUROC appears to be a full-model metric with multiple non-genetic covariates (including family history and smoking/BMI), and no PGS-only AUROC/R2 is provided, so the PRS-specific contribution cannot be cleanly compared across models—lowering certainty to DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL. All 11 listed candidates are direct matches at the disease-concept level (trait_efo=Parkinson disease or closely aligned), but several are progression/dementia endpoints (PGS000056, PGS000211, PGS000777) rather than generic PD risk/status, and some have covariate-heavy full models (e.g., PGS001774 includes multiple non-genetic risk factors including family history; PGS004924 includes environmental exposures), making their reported AUROC less PRS-comparable. Main limitation: across the pool, PRS-only (covariate-free) discrimination metrics are largely absent, and several reported AUROCs are full-model and not directly comparable across differing covariate sets, so the ranking remains moderately uncertain.

All 4 candidates are direct matches to the target concept (peripheral vascular disease) via closely aligned endpoints: two are labeled/phenotyped as “Peripheral vascular disease, unspecified” (PGS001843, PGS002055) and two as “Peripheral artery disease” (PGS005158, PGS005217), which is a closely overlapping clinical entity within peripheral vascular disease. Overall confidence is Moderate (not High) because the best candidate is PAD/incident-focused rather than explicitly “PVD unspecified,” and because comparable PRS-only AUC/R2 metrics are not available across candidates, limiting direct metric-based comparability.

All three candidates are direct-match at the ontology level (trait_efo=preeclampsia), but endpoint fidelity differs. All listed candidates are direct matches to the target trait (prostate cancer / prostate carcinoma) based on trait_reported/trait_efo and generally aligned phenotyping_reported. Direct-match candidates for psoriasis are present (multiple models with trait_efo=psoriasis and phenotyping_reported=Psoriasis). PGS001312 is the best-supported direct match because it has exact endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported: Psoriasis), reports PRS-comparable metrics including PGS-only AUROC (0.69158) and PGS-only R² (0.05226) plus full-model AUROC (0.69754), and uses standard/basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs) with a large UKB training set (n=269,704).
